result.rule: Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.

args.text: When the description states that work proceeds from one activity or phase to another, preserve the stated order by connecting the corresponding BPMN elements with sequence flows, including links into and out of newly begun phases.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing documented guideline already addresses missing sequence flows and transitions between stated activities.

result.rule: Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Keep each flow node and sequence flow inside its owning process or subprocess. Sequence flows never cross pool or subprocess boundaries.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.

result.rule: When the description presents distinct activities in an ordered progression, including transitions into, through, or out of branches or synchronization points: Connect each consecutive activity with a sequence flow, preserving the stated transitions through branches and synchronization points.

When the description states a conditional outcome followed by intervening actions or an approval before a later activity: Model the branch through the described intervening actions and approval in the stated order; do not connect it directly to a later activity that bypasses them.
When the description explicitly states the outcome or condition at which the process ends: Label the end event with that stated outcome rather than a generic or unspecified ending.

When the description states a conditional path but does not specify what happens when the condition is false: If an end event is modeled for that unspecified path, label it neutrally rather than assigning an unstated outcome.
